facts.text: North St. Paul began as Castle, laid out in 1887 by Henry Anson Castle when the Wisconsin Central Railroad reached the spot.
Neumann's Bar, opened in 1887, remains North St. Paul's oldest continuously operating bar, still serving drinks in its historic downtown.
St Mark's Lutheran Church, founded in 1887, stands as one of North St. Paul's earliest religious institutions.
The Catholic Church of St. Peter, with its parochial school on Margaret Street, sits just north of North St. Paul's historic downtown.
The cornerstone of North St. Paul's church was laid in September 1915, and by 1916 the community added stained‑glass windows, pews, a pipe organ, and Italian marble altars.
Silver Lake and Casey Lake, North St. Paul's largest bodies of water, each boast large adjacent parks for outdoor recreation.
